Rashi on Nedarim 36a:10:1.english: Rabbi Zeira said: “A lamb for each father’s house” - Which implies [that] a person brings a Paschal [offering] and slaughters [it] for his minor sons and daughters.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:10:2.hebrew: לאו דאורייתא הוא - להכי, הפריש פסח על חבירו, לא עשה ולא כלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:10:2.english: [It] is not by Torah law - Therefore, [if] one set aside a Paschal lamb for his fellow, he has done nothing at all.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:11:1.hebrew: וממאי - דלאו דאורייתא הוא? מדתנן וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:11:1.english: And from where - [do we know] that it is not by Torah law? From that which we learned, etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:11:2.english: And if you say, "a lamb for a fathers' household" - [meaning] that a person may slaughter [the Paschal lamb] on behalf of his minor children by Torah law.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:11:3.hebrew: על בישרא קאי ומזכי להו - כלומר, היאך יכול זה לזכות את אחיו מאחר שנשחט? והא תנן (פסחים פט.): נמנין ומושכין ידיהן עד שישחט? אלא, אזמוני להו לאחר שחיטה לאו דאורייתא, והך משנה משמע דבבניו קטנים מיירי:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:11:3.english: Does he stand over the meat and acquire [it] for them?! - That is to say: How can this one acquire [a portion] for his brothers after it has been slaughtered? For did we not learn in a Mishnah (Pesachim 89a): "People may register and withdraw their hands until it is slaughtered"? Rather, inviting them [to partake] after slaughter is not [a matter of] Torah law, and this Mishnah implies that it is speaking of his minor sons.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:12:1.hebrew: אלא - הואיל ולאו דאורייתא הוא, למה ליה לאבוהון למימר: "הריני שוחט את הפסח על מי שיעלה מכם לירושלים"? כדי לזרזן במצות:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:12:1.english: Rather - Since it is not by Torah law, why did their father need to say, "I am slaughtering the Paschal lamb for whichever of you ascends [first] to Jerusalem"? [It was] in order to motivate them in [the performance of] mitzvot.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:12:2.hebrew: תניא נמי הכי - כדי לזרזן קאמר. מדקאמר בנים שפלים, ולא קאמר ובנים לא יצאו ידי חובתן, מכלל דלא מחייבי מדאורייתא, אלא לזרזן קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:12:2.english: This is also taught [in a baraita] - [It means that he spoke] in order to motivate them. Since [the baraita] states, "sons [were] lazy," and does not state, "and the sons did not fulfill their obligation," it follows that they are not obligated by Torah law; rather, [it means that he spoke] to motivate them.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:1:1.english: If he was a priest - [Referring to] the one who imposed the vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:1:2.hebrew: יזרוק עליו דם חטאתו ודם אשמו - קתני סתם, דמשמע כל חטאות ואשמות, ואע"ג דלא מחוסרי כפרה נינהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:1:2.english: He may sprinkle on his behalf the blood of his sin-offering and the blood of his guilt-offering - [The Tanna] teaches [this] without qualification, which implies all sin-offerings and guilt-offerings, even though they are not [offerings of] those lacking atonement.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:2:1.hebrew: לא, לעולם שלוחי דידן נינהו, ומאי דם חטאתו ודם אשמו דקתני? חטאתו של מצורע כו', דהיינו מחוסרי כפרה וכו', <abbr title="והוא הדין">וה"ה</abbr> לגדול:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:2:1.english: No, actually they are our agents; and what is "blood of his sin-offering and blood of his guilt-offering" that it taught? The sin-offering of a leper, etc. — that is, [offerings of] those lacking atonement, etc. — and the same applies to an adult.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:3:1.english: [If they did so] intentionally, they are liable - To pay [for] an offering to the owner.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:4:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה - יביא אדם אפי' חטאת חלב על חבירו, שכן מביא קרבן על אשתו שוטה, דמשמע כל קרבנות שהוא חייבת, אפי' אם אכלה חלב: ומתרץ רבי יוחנן: אשתו שוטה היכי דמי שתהא מחויבת קרבן? אי דאכלה כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:4:1.english: But if so - A person should bring even a sin-offering for [eating] forbidden fat on behalf of his fellow, for indeed one brings an offering on behalf of his mentally incompetent wife, which implies all offerings that she is obligated [to bring], even if she ate forbidden fat. And Rabbi Yochanan answers: What is the case of his mentally incompetent wife such that she would be obligated [to bring] an offering? If [it is a case] where she ate [forbidden fat], etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:4:2.english: To [act] properly I appointed you - [as] an agent, and not to [act] improperly.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:5:1.hebrew: אמרי - לעולם שלוחי דידן נינהו, ולהכי פיגולו פיגול:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:5:1.english: They say - Actually, [the priests] are our agents, and therefore his piggul is piggul.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:5:2.english: It will not be imputed to him - It shall be piggul in any case.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:6:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה - יביא אדם אפי' חטאת חלב על חבירו, שכן מביא קרבן על אשתו שוטה, דמשמע כל קרבנות שהיא חייבת, אפי' אם אכלה חלב:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:6:1.english: However, if that is so - let a person bring even a sin-offering [for] forbidden fat on [behalf of] his fellow, just as he brings an offering for his wife who is an imbecile — which implies all offerings that she is obligated [to bring], even if she ate forbidden fat.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:7:1.hebrew: ומתרץ רבי יוחנן אשתו שוטה היכי דמי - שתהא מחויבת קרבן? אי דאכלה כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:7:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan answers: What are the circumstances of his wife who is an imbecile - [such] that she would be obligated [to bring] an offering? If she ate, etc.:

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:8:1.hebrew: פסול - הקרבן, דהואיל ונדחה כשנשתטית, דלאו בת קרבן היא, ידחה. התם נמי גבי אשה, הואיל ונדחית בשעת אכילה, נדחית מהכל, ואין אדם מביא קרבן חלב על אשתו שוטה, וליכא למירמא מהכא. וכי קאמינא דלר' יהודה הא דמביא קרבן על אשתו שוטה, כגון זבה או יולדת או מצורעת:
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:8:1.english: Disqualified - The offering [is disqualified], for since it was rejected when she became an imbecile—as she is not subject to [bringing] an offering—it remains rejected. There too, regarding the woman, since she was rejected at the time of eating, she is rejected from everything, and a man does not bring a [sin-]offering for forbidden fat on behalf of his wife who is an imbecile, and one cannot raise a contradiction from here. And when I say that according to Rabbi Yehudah, that [case where] he brings an offering on behalf of his wife who is an imbecile [refers to] such as a zavah, or a woman after childbirth, or a metzora'at.

Rashi on Nedarim 36a:9:1.hebrew: וקפריך תו יביא אדם כו' - אלמה אמר ר' אלעזר, הפריש פסח על חבירו שלא מדעתו כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 36a:9:1.english: And [the Gemara] asks further: "Let a person bring, etc." - Why did Rabbi Elazar say: "[If one] separated a Paschal lamb on behalf of another without his knowledge, etc."?

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:11:1.hebrew: על בישרא קאי ומזכה להון - בתמיה; כלומר, לאחר שחיטה יכול להמנותם? והא תנן (פסחים דף פט.): "מושכין ידיהן עד שישחטו, אבל לאחר שחיטה לא"! אלמא דהמנאת קטנים לאו דאורייתא, ובניו דקטנים מיירי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:11:1.english: "He stands over the meat and acquires [it] on their behalf" - [This is asked] rhetorically; that is to say, after slaughter, can he register them? Have we not learned in a Mishnah (Pesachim 89a): "They may withdraw their hands [from a Paschal lamb] until it is slaughtered, but after slaughter, [they may] not"! Evidently, the registration of minors is not by Torah law, and "his sons" [in the Mishnah] refers to minors:

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:12:1.english: Regarding minors, why [did he] need to say to them - since they did not register them [on the Paschal lamb]? [In order] to motivate them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:1:1.hebrew: אם היה כהן - אותו המדיר ממנו זורק חטאתו ואשמו, דמשמע ליה דמיירי בחטאת חלב ודם, אלמא שלוחי דרחמנא נינהו. וה"ה דמצי לאותובי ממתני' חטאות ואשמות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:1:1.english: If he was a priest - that [person] who vowed to prohibit [the other from benefiting] from him may sprinkle [the blood of] his sin-offering and his guilt-offering, for it is implied to him that [the Tosefta] is speaking of a sin-offering [brought for] forbidden fat and blood; thus [we see that the priests] are agents of the Merciful One. And the same is true that he could have raised an objection from the Mishnah, [which mentions] sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:4:1.hebrew: אמאי פיגולו פיגול - לימא: לתיקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:4:1.english: Why is his piggul [considered] piggul? - Let [the one bringing the offering] say [to him]: "I sent you to perform [the task] properly, and not to perform [it] improperly."

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:6:1.hebrew: אלמה אמר ר' אלעזר הפריש חטאת חלב וכו' - תימה: מדרבי יוחנן גופיה תיקשי, דהכל צריכין דעת, וצ"ע. וי"ל דמצינן למימר דר' יוחנן מיירי בכהן המקריב, שצריך דעת בעלים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:6:1.english: "Why did Rabbi Elazar say: [One who] separated a sin-offering [for] forbidden fat, etc." - This is astonishing: one could raise a difficulty from Rabbi Yoḥanan himself, [who stated] that "everyone requires knowledge," and this requires further study. One can answer that we can say that Rabbi Yoḥanan is speaking of the kohen who offers [the sacrifice], [meaning] that he requires the knowledge of the owner:

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:7:1.hebrew: שוטה לאו בת קרבן היא - והא דאמר לעיל: "זאת תורת היולדת" — בין פיקחת בין שוטה; מיהו איהו לא מצי מייתי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:7:1.english: An imbecile is not subject to an offering - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] said above: "This is the law of the woman who gives birth" — whether [she is] competent or an imbecile; however, he cannot bring [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:9:1.hebrew: יביא אדם פסח על חבירו שכן אדם מביא קרבן על בניו כשהן קטנים וכו', אמר רבי זירא: שה לבית לאו דאורייתא הוא - כלומר, דקטנים אינם צריכים למנות, דאם אוכלין מן הפסח לא הוי כנאכל שלא למנוייו; דלא אסר רחמנא אלא להנהו דאיתנהו במצות "תכוסו", אבל אותם דלא שייך בהו לא מיירי. מידי דהוה אנשים, דרשות הן — שאע"פ שאין חייבות בפסח, מותרות לאכול ממנו ואינו נקרא שלא למנוייו; וכן בקטנים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 36a:9:1.english: "Let a person bring a Paschal lamb on behalf of his fellow, just as a person brings a sacrifice for his children when they are minors," etc. "Rabbi Zeira said: 'A lamb for a household' is not biblical." - That is to say, minors do not need to be registered [on the Paschal lamb], for if they eat from the Paschal lamb, it is not considered as being eaten by those not registered on it. For the Merciful One only prohibited [this] for those who are included in the commandment of "you shall be counted" [on the lamb], whereas [for] those to whom it does not apply, [Scripture] does not speak [of them]. Just as with women, who are optional [regarding this obligation]: even though they are not obligated in the Paschal lamb, they are permitted to eat from it and it is not called [eaten by] those not registered on it; and so too with minors.
